note: One system, one baseline, three hardening guides, modelled three ways. The point of the scenario is that the three approaches do not differ in what they can express so much as in how many documents it takes to express it, and what the plan of record ends up holding. Every count is either recomputed from a corpus in this repository, read from the NIST profile stored in data/scenario-evidence/, or forced by the OSCAL schemas, and each says which. What the schemas force is stated on the file rows it explains rather than in a section of its own.
title: One system, three hardening guides
summary: A system under NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 at the High baseline, running Ubuntu, PostgreSQL and Microsoft 365, hardened against a published guide for each. The same scenario is modelled in all three approaches, using every OSCAL model except the plan of action and milestones.

excluded_model.reason: It records what was not met and what is being done about it. That is the same document in all three approaches, so it separates none of them.

hardening.label: CIS Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Benchmark
hardening.derivation: count of steps titled 'Audit for ...' in Easy Dynamics/Center for Internet Security/CIS_Ubuntu_Linux_24_04_LTS_Benchmark_v2_OSCAL_AP.json. The file carries 616 steps, one audit and one remediation for each recommendation, in 53 activities.

hardening.label: DISA STIG PostgreSQL 16
hardening.derivation: count of props step-type=check in Easy Dynamics/DISA/STIG_XCCDF to OSCAL Assessment Plans/postgres16.json. The file carries 111 activities and 222 steps, one check and one remediate for each.
hardening.source: Easy Dynamics/DISA/STIG_XCCDF to OSCAL Assessment Plans/postgres16.json

hardening.derivation: count of steps in Easy Dynamics/CISA BOD 25-01/ap-cisa-scuba-agnostic.json, which carries 128 steps across 7 activities, one activity per Microsoft 365 service.

items_note: One entry per file, so a reader can follow a particular document from the figure into the list beneath it. The names are shortened to fit a tile. Where a model has more than one kind of file in it, the kind is named too: a component definition holding the thing being configured is software, and one holding the checks that test it is validation, which is the distinction the whole approach rests on and is invisible from the file count alone.
